t: #2640 — Find the Score of All Prefixes of an Array
o: conver[i] = nums[i] + max(nums[0..i]); the score of a prefix is the sum of its conver values. We must output the score of every prefix. For [2,3,7,5,10] the scores are [4,10,24,36,56]. Since each prefix's score extends the previous one by exactly one conver value, a single running-max pass suffices.
k: The prefix maximum is maintained in O(1) per step.
Values up to 1e9 and n up to 1e5 mean scores reach ~1e14, requiring 64-bit integers.

a.n: Approach 1: Running max and running score
a.i: Scan left to right keeping the current prefix maximum mx and the accumulated score s. At each element, update mx, add nums[i] + mx to s, and append s to the answer.
s: Initialize mx = 0 (values are positive) and s = 0.
For each x: mx = max(mx, x); s += x + mx; push s.
a.t: O(n) — a single pass with O(1) work per element.
a.sp: O(1) extra beyond the output array.

w: Straightforward prefix-sum exercise; the only real concern is overflow (use long/BigInt semantics — JS numbers are safe here since 1e5·2e9 = 2e14 < 2⁵³). A follow-up might ask for conver of subarrays, which needs a sparse table or monotonic stack.
